reason: Three narrow Eventar security skills (server-action write gates, sign-out through one helper, rate limits feeding the abuse tier) are one class: the auth and session guards every write and sign-out must pass. Merged into one umbrella; the detailed rules and the backtest facts move to references.

Full-stack security audit on 2026-11-04 shows three repeated pitfalls: an empty-input shortcut sitting ahead of requireStaff, a confirmed-email check wrongly placed in the deny-only getStaffSessionState (6 test failures, reverted), and a new auth field that broke staff fixtures across three test files. The existing skill covers gates and sign-out but not these ordering and deny-versus-grant rules.

The user-lens review found that an unconfirmed staff-matching session redirected to /dashboard would loop between /login and /dashboard. The fix (redirect to /login?error=email_unconfirmed, render the form, skip the staff lookup) is a durable rule for any refused-login redirect in Eventar.

Ivan ruled the role matrix in this episode and the inventory showed the DB write gates check org only, not role or creator. The existing auth-session-guards skill governs write gates and is the one that was in play, so the rule goes here as a patch, labelled as not yet built.

The line "This is NOT yet built" is superseded: the trigger now exists in a local migration. Also records two guard-design rules found in the dev review: check both sides of an UPDATE, and the narrow self-claim exemption.
Stale statement: the Q51 app-side helpers and bulk refusal were built and tested this episode, so "still to follow" now misleads the next session. Reconciled to the built state.

New durable technique from this episode: the role-rights change was only safe because the write-path inventory surfaced surprises (storage bucket, role-less RPCs, email) that a rule-by-rule edit would have missed. Attached to the skill that governs write gates.

The Q52 change made the DB identity function require a confirmed auth row. Any test that fakes a JWT without sub and a confirmed auth.users row now silently sees zero rows, which the existing getUser-fixture bullet does not cover. This is a new guard on the grant side that the skill must name.

The sign-out check read document.cookie and reported the session cookie gone. document.cookie hides HttpOnly cookies, so the empty list proves nothing about the server session. The skill has no browser storage probe and no warning about this gap.

Fold two narrow project guards into the auth and session umbrella: link-key edits (same predicate as the claim) and staff email on two orgs (PGRST116 tri-state). Both are write-gate or lookup-gate rules; siblings deleted after this lands.
Insert the link-key-edit and staff-email subsections absorbed from the two sibling guards, before the rate-limit section.

Reconcile the flat "every sign-out goes through the helper" rule with two live inline call sites. The trace shows the assistant found them and declined a silent swap; the rule must say so, or the next session either trips on the mismatch or swaps them without the UX check.

Dev-lens review of 2a7a496 flagged that an optional permission flag on the dashboard row type fails open: an omitted writable gives the blue Check-in and Edit. The existing auth-guard skill covers server gates and display helpers but not the optional-flag typing trap, so this extends its role-gate section.

Ivan ruled on 2026-11-22 that on-the-day check-in and walk-ins are open to every org member, overriding the Q51 event-writer rule for door actions. The live skill still states only the Q51 rule, and the assistant offered body_admin/auditor splits he had not named, which he rejected.

The door-action bullet and role-split bullet are now stale: UX-R8 was ruled and committed locally as e45e45f, and body_admin now counts for the door. The 2026-11-06 Q51 line still says body_admin cannot check in. Patch points the old rule at the new ruling so the library stops contradicting itself.

Door bullet still says the rule is unbuilt and that mark_attended and the guard triggers refuse members. UX-R8 is committed as e45e45f and the new can_run_door migration exists. Rewriting the bullet to the ruling and the built state stops the next session from reverting a finished change.

The instruction to ask about body_admin and auditor is superseded by Ivan's explicit ruling, and leaving it would make a future session re-ask a settled question. Ivan had objected to repeated role-split options.

Widening a role gate on the door desk (UX-R8) changed the page's write path but not the read RPC the same page calls. body_admin got a working desk while the eligibility RPC still refused that role, so every load showed a false outage banner. The inventory rule covers write paths only; it must also cover read RPCs the page calls.

A role gate widened to a new role was proven on one table (checkin) only. Sibling speaker tables still required the staff's own organisation in RLS, and the door branch of the event-writer guard let a colleague's row carry forged attribution. Both were found by review after the green suite, so the per-table, per-role probe and the attribution pin belong in this skill.
